mechanism_log: The system has 6 active inputs (X1-X6) and 6 inert inputs (X7-X12). The output structure is sparse: Y3 depends only on X1 and X3 (with strong concave nonlinearity in X1). Y4 depends primarily on X2, X4, and X6 (with weak X1 contribution). Y1 and Y2 depend on all 6 active inputs. X3 and X4 are 'universally beneficial' (improve all objectives simultaneously). X2 creates a Y1/Y4 vs Y2 trade-off. X6 creates a Y1 vs Y2/Y4 conflict. Y1's linear R²=0.72 suggests significant nonlinearity or interactions remain unexplored.

The system has 6 active inputs (X1-X6) and 6 inert ones (X7-X12). Setting X1=X3=X4=1.0 is universally beneficial. X5 has a saturating positive effect on Y1 only (gradient drops to zero at X5=1.0). The main Pareto trade-off is controlled by X2 and X6. Y1 has a massive X2×X4 interaction: both high together gives Y1>1.1. A critical discovery is that X6's effect on Y2 REVERSES sign depending on X2: at high X2 (≥0.8), X6 actually decreases Y2 (beneficial), while at low X2 it increases Y2 (harmful). This X2×X6 interaction on Y2 was completely missed by the linear model. Y3 depends only on X1 and X3 (confirmed Y3=0.997 at X1=X3=1). Y4 depends on X2 (strong positive), X4 (moderate positive), and X6 (negative). The new 12-point grid at X1=X3=X4=X5=1 completely dominates the previous Pareto front built from midpoint OAT sweeps.

X6→Y2 sign reversal: At X2=1.0, increasing X6 from 0.1→1.0 DECREASES Y2 from 0.362 to 0.303. At X2=0.3, increasing X6 from 0.1→0.5 INCREASES Y2 from 0.116 to 0.167. Strong X2×X6 interaction on Y2.

surprises: Y1 predictions were systematically low by 0.03-0.35 at the extreme corners. The interaction effects are much stronger than gradient-based linear extrapolation suggested. Y1=1.13 vs my prediction of 0.80.

Y4 prediction error at X2=0.1 was -0.094: Y4=0.036 vs predicted 0.13. The Y4 model overestimates at low X2, suggesting X2→Y4 is nonlinear (convex) with most gains at higher X2.
